title: Research: Where can you still get HIFLD infrastructure data now that HIFLD Open is gone?

labels.name: agent:research
labels.description: Research issue (reading or spike), worked by a Research worker

body:
Card: https://app.notion.com/p/3fccc69045cb813baaa6edfb6492ea3f

**Card:** https://app.notion.com/p/3fccc69045cb813baaa6edfb6492ea3f (founder-asked, article) · Reading research, no branch or PR.

## Argument
Where can a GIS analyst, planner or developer now get the HIFLD layers they used to download from HIFLD Open? We expect three answers:
- Most open layers are preserved in HIFLD Next.
- Some are maintained again by their source agencies, such as EIA, FEMA, DOT/BTS, USACE and NCES.
- A few have no public copy anywhere.

Nobody has yet said in one place which layer falls into which group.

## What would settle it
- **DHS/CISA's notices on the shutdown.** Find the date, the stated reason, and where they pointed users (HIFLD Secure, the source agencies). Archived copies of the HIFLD Open catalog give the list of former layers.
- **HIFLD Next against that list.** Compare the HIFLD Next catalog (layers, bulk files, API, MCP server) with the former list: how many layers are preserved, and how current each copy is.
- **The source agencies' own portals.** For the most-used layer groups (energy, transportation, emergency services, schools, hospitals, water), check whether each agency publishes a maintained version, and the date of its latest data.
- **What is gone.** List the layers that came from licensed or restricted data and now sit only behind HIFLD Secure, or nowhere.
- **The strongest case against.** Check whether other mirrors (Esri Living Atlas, data.gov, academic or community archives) already answer this question, or whether agency replacements are so complete that a consolidated guide adds little.

Write from our experience; don't speak for PEDP.

## Done means
- Evidence for, Evidence against and Verdict rewritten on the card in the Writing a proposal format: Argument, Why it matters, What would settle it, Evidence for, Evidence against, Our standing, Verdict, Score line.
- At least three solid sources, including at least one primary source.
- Each new source added to Finds and related to the card.
- A two- or three-sentence Verdict on this issue.
